categories.title: Type Safety

source_requirement.statement: Eliminate 25% of type safety violations. Every fix must preserve existing functionality; all tests still pass. Superficial fixes do not count. Replacing any with unknown without proper type narrowing is not an improvement; fixes must include correct, meaningful types that reflect the actual data.

fields.strict_mode_error_count_note: N/A because strict mode is enabled.

top_violation_dense_files.why_problematic: High-risk route boundary code mixed request input, JSONB document properties, database rows, and API responses, so unsafe casts or non-null assertions could become runtime contract bugs.
Project route code shaped document-backed project responses from loosely typed PostgreSQL rows and properties, making route/API drift hard for TypeScript to catch.
Issue routes sit on the core issue/document boundary and previously relied on casts around request bodies, associations, properties, and list/detail response shaping.
The unified document page bridges routed document types, editor state, and API responses; loose typing here can misroute editor views or hide document-shape mismatches.
Seed data drives local audit/test scenarios; dense non-null assertions can mask invalid fixture assumptions and make evidence setup brittle.

notes: The audit deliverable asks for total counts; production counts are included in measurements because they are useful for judging source-risk reduction.
Strict mode is a configuration finding, not a syntax-count measurement.

measurements.label: Latest implicit any and untyped parameter report

claims.statement: Total counted type-safety syntax decreased from 1340 to 625, a 53.4% reduction, clearing the 25% source requirement.
limits: This is a syntax-count denominator, not a semantic type-risk score.
Production counted syntax decreased 55.7%, which is useful context but separate from the total-count source gate.
Production any usage decreased from 94 to 1; production non-null assertions decreased from 325 to 36 after the authenticated-route context sweep.

`pnpm type-safety:report` shows 0 tsc implicit-any diagnostics, but 47 production unannotated parameters still infer to any from any-typed parents; this is residual follow-up work and not part of the official syntax-count reduction claim.

evidence.description: Category 1 methodology defines the TypeScript AST counter used as the official denominator.
Improvement report records type-check passing after structural boundary changes and the meaningful `as` cast reduction pass.
Full API test suite passed after the meaningful `as` cast reduction pass.
Full web test suite passed after the meaningful `as` cast reduction pass.

Category 1 work centered on shared boundary schemas, route aliases derived from @ship/shared, request validation, typed client/server contracts, API query coercion, approval JSONB guards, API status errors, and API-response-to-editor mappers rather than replacing any with unknown.

evidence.result: 0 tsc implicit-any diagnostics; 47 production unannotated params inferred as any
evidence.description: Full report covers source-text items beyond the audit deliverable table: compiler implicit-any diagnostics and untyped parameters that infer to any from any-typed parents.

caveats: ESLint warning counts are useful as a worklist but are not the official before/after denominator.
Replacing any with unknown without meaningful narrowing is not counted as a real improvement.

Untyped parameters inferred as any are measured by `pnpm type-safety:report` and remain follow-up work; the official closeout claim is the source-required 25% reduction in counted type-safety syntax plus passing tests.
non_claims: Does not claim production counted syntax alone clears the 25% threshold.
Does not claim all syntax categories carry equal semantic risk.
Does not claim every untyped callback parameter has been eliminated.

fix_records.title: CSRF failures return JSON 403
fix_records.repro_steps: Attempt a state-changing document request with an expired/missing CSRF token.
fix_records.before_behavior: The failure could fall through to HTML/Express error output, confusing API/UI callers.
fix_records.after_behavior: The API returns a JSON 403 envelope and the editor remains usable.
fix_records.user_impact: Prevents confusing server-output leakage during an auth/session edge case.

fix_records.title: Backlinks offline/degraded state preserves context
fix_records.repro_steps: Open a document with backlinks context, then force the backlinks request/network path offline or failing.
fix_records.before_behavior: Backlinks failures were console-only and the UI could silently lose context.
fix_records.after_behavior: The UI preserves the last successful context and shows stale/offline/degraded status.
fix_records.user_impact: Reduces user confusion and avoids apparent data/context loss while offline.

fix_records.title: AI unavailable degraded mode
fix_records.repro_steps: Run the app without usable Bedrock/AWS credentials and open a weekly plan quality banner.
fix_records.before_behavior: AI analysis unavailability could become noisy server failure or a disappearing/unclear assistant state.
fix_records.after_behavior: AI status and analysis endpoints return controlled ai_unavailable JSON without invoking Bedrock when credentials are missing (guard test: api/src/services/__tests__/ai-analysis.test.ts); PlanQualityBanner/RetroQualityBanner use shared useAiQuality + QualityBannerShell and show a concise unavailable state while keeping editor content and persisted analysis visible.
fix_records.user_impact: Prevents confusion when provider credentials are missing and avoids clearing user/editor context.

verified_vulnerability_fixes.vulnerability_class: Local file upload validation and browser-executable inline serving
verified_vulnerability_fixes.reproduction_steps: Before: run pnpm security:probe -- --probe input-file-upload-size-mismatch --run-id before-file-size and pnpm security:probe -- --probe input-file-serve-headers --run-id before-file-headers. The first accepted mismatched bytes; the second served uploaded HTML with inline Content-Disposition.
verified_vulnerability_fixes.fix_applied: api/src/routes/files.ts now rejects local-upload bodies whose byte length differs from files.size_bytes and serves user uploads as attachments with sanitized filenames while retaining X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
verified_vulnerability_fixes.proof: Before reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-file-size/report.json and my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-file-headers/report.json. After reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-file-size/report.json and my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-file-headers-2/report.json. Final full report: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/latest.json.

verified_vulnerability_fixes.reproduction_steps: Before: run pnpm security:probe -- --probe websocket-malformed-frame --run-id before-ws-malformed. The probe reported unsafe malformed-frame handling; the first full probe attempt also exposed an unhandled ws oversized-frame error in the dev server log.
verified_vulnerability_fixes.fix_applied: api/src/collaboration/index.ts now catches collaboration message decode failures, closes unsupported/invalid collaboration and events messages with 1003, and handles oversized ws frames with 1009 without crashing the API process.
verified_vulnerability_fixes.proof: Before report: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/before-ws-malformed/report.json. After reports: my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-ws-malformed/report.json, my-docs/evidence/security-audit/runs/after-ws-oversized/report.json, and final deterministic close-code evidence in my-docs/evidence/security-audit/latest.json.
